text:
Tara: Quick heads-up — ran a full perf sweep on the new token-budget batcher. Observed regression on long-context paged-attn cases. Attaching summary below.

Michael: Top-line numbers? p50/p99/tokens-sec?

Tara: p50 +12% latency, p99 +22% at seq_len=2048. Tokens/sec median fell ~540k -> ~470k on A100 for chat workloads. nvprof shows higher SMEM bank conflicts and lowered SM eff occupancy for flash_paged_v2.

Jin: Any change in KV cache hit-rate? If batcher groups prefixes more, we might be increasing per-request KV working set and SMEM pressure.

Tara: KV hit-rate actually up from 0.62 to 0.68 (more shared prefixes). BUT we added a per-request pointer table in the paged kernel path which increased per-CTA SMEM from ~48KB -> ~56KB. That seems to be the tipping point.

Samir: 56KB/CTA on our CUDA arch drops active warps — occupancy halves. Bank conflicts + lower occupancy explains the tokens/sec loss. Two levers: shrink SMEM usage (pack/move pointer table) or route these batches to a different kernel variant.

Anya: Scheduler heuristic idea:
```
if seq_len >= 1536 and kv_hit_rate >= 0.6:
  kernel = flash_fused_low_smem
else:
  kernel = flash_paged_v2
```
flash_fused_low_smem keeps SMEM <32KB at cost of some extra instructions — should maintain occupancy for big seqs.

Michael: Run an A/B microbench 200 runs each for seq 512/1024/1536/2048 comparing paged_v2 vs fused_low_smem and post results to #eng-runtime-bench.

ops-bot: automated-bench: run_id=bench-2026-03-05-09:23 kernelA=flash_paged_v2 kernelB=flash_fused_low_smem
results (tokens/sec median):
- seq512: paged=580k, fused_low=540k
- seq1024: paged=560k, fused_low=545k
- seq1536: paged=500k, fused_low=520k
- seq2048: paged=470k, fused_low=510k
error bars ~3%

Tara: fused_low wins for >=1536 as predicted. nvprof traces show pipeline stalls at stage 2 due to SMEM serialization and many bank conflicts for paged_v2.

Jin: For the pointer table, can we pack to 32-bit indices and compute global offsets in-kernel instead of storing 64-bit pointers? That saves bytes per request (approx 8 bytes * requests_per_CTA). Also consider spilling small metadata to global memory with coalesced accesses.

Samir: Bigger opportunity: adjust tiling. Current tile_w=64, tile_h=16 for paged. If we try tile_w=48, tile_h=16 we reduce SMEM scratch for partial reductions and lower bank stride. Also try increasing pipeline stages from 3 -> 4 to better hide global loads. I'll run conflict counters after changing tiles.

Anya: Also propose runtime fallback: monitor "effective occupancy" = active_warps / max_warps and if measured occupancy < 0.6 for two consecutive windows, switch kernel for that route. Pseudopatch:
```
- route_by: latency
+ kernel_selector:
+  - cond: seq_len >= 1536 and kv_hit_rate >= 0.6
+    kernel: flash_fused_low_smem
+  - fallback: flash_paged_v2
+  - monitor: occupancy < 0.6 -> switch to fused_low
```
This keeps normal routing but provides quick mitigation when a kernel's occupancy collapses.

Michael: We should also add an "effective occupancy" metric to Console (per-model/per-kernel windowed) so regressions are visible in the UI. Add to backlog.

Tara: Action items:
- Jin/Samir: pack pointer table + try tile_w=48, pipeline=4 (owner: Jin)
- Samir: bench tile changes + collect nvprof SMEM_BANK_CONFLICTS traces (owner: Samir)
- Anya: scheduler PR implementing seq+kv heuristic + occupancy fallback + rollout plan (owner: Anya)
- Michael: add occupancy metric to Console backlog (owner: Michael)

Michael: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: created ticket PERF-1372 and linked this thread.

Tara: NVPROF excerpt for quick reference:
```
SM_EFF_OCCUPANCY: paged_v2=0.42, fused_low=0.78
SMEM_BANK_CONFLICTS: paged_v2=230k, fused_low=18k
```
Kernel launch sample:
```
paged_v2 <<<blocks=64, threads=256, smem=57344>>>  (~56KB/CTA)
fused_low <<<blocks=128, threads=256, smem=28672>>> (~28KB/CTA)
```
